examples.title: SaaS Free-Trial Removal
examples.problem: B2B CRM software company facing low conversion rates (2%) from free trials due to customer setup inertia.
examples.assets: Software code, sales team, customer support, user onboarding process, customer data.
examples.perception: A free trial is mandatory to convince buyers to test features before paying.
examples.manipulation: Remove the 14-day self-service free trial completely.
examples.concept: A high-friction software sign-up flow with no self-service access, requiring upfront commitment.
examples.adaptation: Eliminated trial tire-kickers. Replaced trial with a 30-minute personalized ROI consultation and mandatory live onboarding upon payment.
examples.results: Conversion rate jumped from 2% to 18%, average deal size increased 40%, customer lifetime value doubled due to proper onboarding.

examples.title: Retail Store Cashier Elimination
examples.problem: Urban convenience store struggling with high cashier wage overhead and long checkout lines during morning rush hours.
examples.assets: Store inventory, shelf sensors, cameras, mobile app, store floor, customers.
examples.perception: Every retail transaction requires a human cashier or self-checkout barcode scanning terminal.
examples.manipulation: Subtract the cashier and physical checkout terminals from the store environment.
examples.concept: A retail store where customers walk in, grab items, and exit directly through the door with zero checkout interaction.
examples.adaptation: Sensors and mobile app tracking bill the customer's account automatically upon exit (Grab-and-Go model).
examples.results: Reduced labor overhead by 65%, increased morning rush throughput by 300%, expanded store operating hours to 24/7.

examples.title: E-Commerce Packaging Subtraction

examples.manipulation: Subtract the outer cardboard shipping box completely.
examples.concept: A shipping label stuck directly onto the item's reusable protective inner bag.
examples.adaptation: Engineered heavy-duty, tamper-evident recycled polymer shipping bags that serve as both garment protection and outer shipping container.
examples.results: Lowered packaging unit costs by 70%, reduced shipping volume weight by 35%, improved customer brand sustainability rating.

examples.title: Restaurant Menu Subtraction

examples.adaptation: Fixed nightly multi-course tasting menu curated daily based on seasonal market availability.
examples.results: Food waste dropped to near 0%, kitchen prep time reduced by 50%, gross food margins expanded by 28% while creating an exclusive dining experience.

examples.adaptation: Implemented automated SLA routing: Critical enterprise issues get 15-minute response; low-tier minor requests get 24-hour SLA.
examples.results: Enterprise customer retention reached 99%, overall support team operational stress dropped, ticket backlog decreased by 60%.

examples.title: Occupancy-Dependent Hotel Room Pricing
examples.problem: Hotel losing revenue due to static room rates leaving rooms empty on weekdays while underpricing weekend peaks.
examples.assets: Room inventory, booking calendar, local event database, historic demand data, dynamic pricing engine.
examples.perception: Hotel room rates are fixed per season (e.g., Summer rate vs. Winter rate).
examples.manipulation: Create a dependency between night room rate and current real-time hotel occupancy percentage.
examples.concept: A booking engine where room rates automatically rise incrementally as remaining room availability shrinks.
examples.adaptation: Deployed automated yield management algorithm adjusting room prices continuously based on occupancy velocity.
examples.results: RevPAR (Revenue Per Available Room) increased by 22%, hotel average occupancy rose from 68% to 86%.

examples.title: Expiration-Dependent Grocery Markdown
examples.problem: Supermarket chain losing millions on spoiled fresh produce and dairy discarded past expiration dates.
examples.assets: Product inventory, digital shelf edge tags, shelf life data, pricing software.
examples.perception: Product price remains static until the item expires and is thrown away by store clerks.
examples.manipulation: Create a dependency between product price and remaining days until shelf expiration.
examples.concept: Digital price tags that automatically discount items incrementally as they near expiration.
examples.adaptation: Installed smart digital shelf labels that reduce price by 20% at 3 days to expiry, and 50% at 1 day to expiry.
examples.results: Food spoilage waste reduced by 70%, recovering $540,000 annually in previously lost inventory margins.

examples.title: Speed-Dependent Freight Shipping Rates
examples.problem: Express courier service facing bottlenecked air freight capacity during peak holiday shipping rushes.
examples.assets: Cargo plane space, delivery speed commitments, shipping rates, parcel weight.
examples.perception: Delivery pricing is based purely on package weight and distance tier.
examples.manipulation: Create a dependency between shipping price and client-selected delivery speed flexibility window.
examples.concept: A shipping model where customers receive sliding-scale discounts for allowing 3-day flexible delivery windows.
examples.adaptation: Offered 'Flexible Economy' tier allowing logistics algorithms to route packages via cheaper ground transport during peak air spikes.
examples.results: Smoothed peak air cargo demand, reduced expensive third-party charter plane rentals, improved net fleet profit margins by 19%.

examples.title: Time-of-Day Electricity Billing Dependency
examples.problem: Electric utility grid suffering from extreme peak load surges during summer afternoons requiring expensive peaker plant operation.
examples.assets: Smart power meters, power grid, electricity pricing engine, commercial/residential consumers.
examples.perception: Electricity cost per kilowatt-hour is flat and static 24 hours a day.
examples.manipulation: Create a dependency between electricity rate per kWh and time of day (Peak vs. Off-Peak grid demand).
examples.concept: A power billing model where electricity is 3x more expensive during 2 PM-7 PM peak, but ultra-cheap overnight.
examples.adaptation: Introduced Time-of-Use (TOU) dynamic pricing meters, incentivizing users to run heavy appliances overnight.
examples.results: Shifted 18% of peak grid load to overnight off-peak hours, avoiding $15M in new peaker power plant capital expenditure.

examples.title: Customer Tenure Loyalty Discount Dependency
examples.problem: Subscription streaming service suffering high customer churn at the 6-month mark as initial promotional discounts expire.
examples.assets: Subscriber database, billing system, loyalty points, tenure length.
examples.perception: Subscription price remains constant or increases after initial sign-up promo period.
examples.manipulation: Create a dependency between monthly subscription pricing and continuous customer tenure duration.
examples.concept: A subscription tier where monthly price decreases or unlocked extra perks increase the longer a user stays subscribed.
examples.adaptation: Implemented 'Tenure Rewards': subscription price drops by 5% every 6 months of continuous membership up to 25%.
examples.results: Customer churn rate decreased by 42%, extending average customer lifetime value (LTV) from 8 months to 26 months.

examples.title: Skill-Level Dependent Software UI Complexity
examples.problem: Design software company suffering high initial churn because novice users find the complex pro toolbar overwhelming.
examples.assets: Software interface, user telemetry analytics, feature toolbars, user account profiles.
examples.perception: Software interface layout is identical for all users regardless of experience level.
examples.manipulation: Create a dependency between displayed user interface complexity and total user app usage hours / skill level.
examples.concept: A software interface that starts ultra-simple for beginners and dynamically unlocks advanced tools as the user gains mastery.
examples.adaptation: Engineered adaptive UI that defaults to basic essential tools for new sign-ups, unlocking pro power tools as user completes tasks.
examples.results: New user 30-day retention jumped from 24% to 68%, reducing onboarding churn drastically while retaining pro capabilities.
